source: The game's own battle code: RpgStateUtils (DEF curve, resist roll), ElementExtensions (element rules), DamageUtils; constants read from the disassembly or called in game.

notes: The multiplier depends only on the defender's DEF: every hit is reduced by the same percentage, whatever its size (1000 DEF = x0.846 on a 1,000 or a 2,000 hit).
DEF can never reduce a hit by more than 85% (floor 0.15).
Boss DEF above 3,000 (e.g. Ulgorim stage 20, 11,000) uses the same curve.

unconfirmed: The 0.15 floor and 5000 scale are fitted to the game's outputs (exact to 6 decimals at every sample), not read from config.

debuffLanding: which stat feeds the target 'resist bonus' and attacker 'accuracy bonus' terms (two F64 fields on the battle state), and the exact corruption types (read as type 11 on the target and Mindfog on the attacker).
Whether the in-skill cast chance ('20% chance to cast') is rolled before and separately from this resist roll (it is a separate script block, so most likely yes).

Status effects: the 1 - X% / 1 + X% mapping is read from the effect's StatType and sign, not traced through the stat code; how two effects of the same type stack (the game usually keeps the strongest) is not decoded.

damageMultiplier.lightDark: Light/Dark attacker vs a non-Light/Dark target: x1.15 if the player-advantage flag is positive, else x1.0. Non-Light/Dark attacker vs a Light/Dark target: x0.85 if that flag is negative, else x1.0.

critChanceDelta.lightDark: -25 when a non-Light/Dark attacker hits a Light/Dark target with a negative player-advantage flag

debuffApplicationChance.lightDark: +10 for a Light/Dark attacker vs a non-Light/Dark target with a positive player-advantage flag; -25 for the reverse case with a negative flag
debuffApplicationChance.source: ElementExtensions.GetDebuffApplicationChanceByElements (percentage points, subtracted from the resist chance)

elements.ignoreElementAdvantage: Effects with ignoreElement get none of these modifiers.
elements.pvp: In PvP, Light and Dark counter each other (in-game PvP hint); GetBasicAdvantageSign handles the pairing.

debuffLanding.rule: resisted if resistChance > random(0..100); otherwise the debuff lands
debuffLanding.resistChance: curve(target RES - attacker ACC) + target resist bonus - attacker accuracy bonus - elements.debuffApplicationChance - corruption(target, type 11) + corruption(attacker, Mindfog)
debuffLanding.curve: stat_curves.json ResistChance_ResMinusAcc (index = RES - ACC + 1500): 0 at equal, 50 at +50, 89.6 at +100, 129 at +200, 244 at +1500; negative when ACC is higher
debuffLanding.floorCap: No floor or cap in the roll itself: resistChance <= 0 always lands, >= 100 is always resisted.
debuffLanding.skipped: Allies' effects are never resisted (same team). Effects marked Unresistable / CanBeResisted = false (skill_mechanics.json) skip the roll.

steps: source damage (CalculateSourceDamage): skill multipliers x stats, crit roll, element damage multiplier

mitigation.normal: effectiveDEF = targetDEF x max(0, defenseFactor - ignoreDefense); damage = round(source x defense.formula(effectiveDEF) x damageTakenFactor x incomingDamageFactor)
mitigation.bleedAndBurn: damage = round(source x incomingDamageFactor x damageTakenFactor): DEF does not apply
mitigation.corruption: damage = round(source x corruptionCoef x incomingDamageFactor), corruptionCoef = CorruptionCoefReducedWithTolerance(target tolerance): Tolerance reduces Corruption damage
mitigation.invincible: a target with an invincibility flag takes 0 from Bleed/Burn

terms.defenseFactor: multiplier on the target's DEF (1 normally; DEF Down debuffs lower it)
terms.ignoreDefense: the hit's IgnoreDefensePercent / 100, clamped to 0..1, subtracted from defenseFactor
terms.damageTakenFactor: target's damage-taken multiplier (e.g. Decrease Damage Taken, Weaken)

mitigation.rounding: to the nearest whole number at the end

crit.chancePct: round(100 x max(0, attacker crit rate + the hit's ModifyCritChancePercent / 100)) + elements.critChanceDelta
crit.roll: crit if random integer 0..999 < 10 x chancePct (so chancePct is a plain percentage; element disadvantage -50 points)
crit.multiplier: 1 + max(0, attacker crit damage + the hit's ModifyCritDamagePercent / 100)  (crit damage stat as a fraction: 0.5 = +50%)
crit.order: source damage = base x critMultiplier x element damage multiplier
exceptions: Corruption damage (damage types 5-16: Mindfog ... Nightmare) never crits and ignores element: source = base.
Hits flagged no-crit (DamageOrHealEvent flag 8) never crit; OnlyCritDamage forces a crit.

statusEffects.DEF Down / DEF Up: BuffStat blocks with StatType Defense (EffectType DebuffDefense / BuffDefense) and an integer percent: they change the target's DEF multiplier, i.e. hit.mitigation defenseFactor = 1 - DEF Down% (or 1 + DEF Up%) / 100.
statusEffects.Weaken: EffectType DebuffDamageTaken on StatType DecreaseDamageTaken (negative): damageTakenFactor = 1 + Weaken% / 100.
statusEffects.Decrease Damage Taken (buff): EffectType BuffDamageTaken on DecreaseDamageTaken: damageTakenFactor = 1 - X% / 100.
statusEffects.amounts: the percent comes from the skill (skill_mechanics.json byLevel tables / the skill text), not from a global table.
statusEffects.source: skill scripts (BuffStat blocks: Category, StatType, EffectType)

instinct.effect: Instinct does not change damage or crit. It is the chance an Invoker not under manual control dodges a danger zone (and switches targets correctly in some encounters): CharacterUtils.DoInstinctCheck rolls stat_curves.json InstinctFactorPct01 (0.3 at rating 0, 1.0 at high ratings).
instinct.inGameText: Improves AI decision-making during battle. Increases the chance to dodge dangerous zones and correctly switch targets in certain encounters.
